title: The Fermionic Cohomology Problem on the Full Fock Space Is $\mathrm{QMA}_1$-Complete
abstract: Fermionic cohomology characterizes the zero-energy states of the supersymmetric Hamiltonian associated with a fermionic differential. Previous work showed that the problem restricted to a particle-number sector specified with the input is $\mathrm{QMA}_1$-hard and belongs to $\mathrm{QMA}$. We study the global problem, in which no sector is specified and cohomology may occur anywhere in the full Fock space. This formulation directly matches the whole-space ground-state question: a specified-degree NO instance may still have zero-energy states in another sector, whereas the global NO promise excludes them across all sectors and their superpositions. We prove that this full-Fock problem is $\mathrm{QMA}_1$-complete for differentials given as exact lists of local monomials, even when each monomial acts on at most $41$ modes. As a companion result, we prove $\mathrm{QMA}_1$-completeness for the specified-degree problem with $30$-mode terms whose hard instances admit a one-dimensional block-chain realization.
summary: This paper proves that determining the fermionic cohomology on the entire Fock space is $\mathrm{QMA}_1$-complete. It achieves this by mapping the physical problem onto a quantum computational hardness problem using advanced techniques involving differential operators and number-penalized lifts. This result establishes a fundamental computational barrier for solving zero-energy state problems in fermionic quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the computational complexity of determining if the fermionic cohomology is non-zero on the entire, full Fock space.
main_result: The global fermionic cohomology problem on the full Fock space is proven to be $\mathrm{QMA}_1$-complete.
method: The proof involves constructing a reduction from known $\mathrm{QMA}_1$-hard problems by lifting the problem structure to the full Fock space using number-penalized techniques and analyzing the resulting Laplacian operator.
model_or_system: The system involves fermionic differential operators ($D$) acting on the full Fock space ($\mathcal{F}n$), which are related to the zero-energy states of an associated supersymmetric Hamiltonian. The structure is built upon marker differentials and data block encoding.
key_observables: The Betti number ($b_p$), which equals the zero-energy degeneracy of the Laplacian ($\Delta_p$), and the existence of non-zero cohomology classes.
important_parameters: The complexity class $\mathrm{QMA}_1$, the maximum number of modes a monomial acts on (e.g., $\le 41$), and the gap ($\delta$) in the Hamiltonian spectrum.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the exact verification convention of $\mathrm{QMA}_1$ and the ability to construct specific, sparse, and well-conditioned residual relations ($eR_ ullet$).

paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical problem (cohomology) to establishing the complexity class (QMA1) by first analyzing the specified-degree case, and finally generalizing the result to the full-Fock space using number-penalized lifts and explicit encoding schemes.
why_interesting: This work connects abstract algebraic topology (cohomology) in quantum many-body systems directly to the computational complexity class $\mathrm{QMA}_1$, providing a powerful tool for classifying the hardness of ground-state problems in quantum physics.
